    params = forward.init(next(rng), emb, mask)
    params = self._zero_mlps(params)
    out = forward.apply(params, next(rng), emb, mask)
    # The last (masked) position should not affect the first two outputs,
    # and outputs at first two positions should be equal (same input,
    # uniform attention).
    np.testing.assert_allclose(out[0, 0], out[0, 1], atol=1e-5)

  def test_causal_mask(self):
    @hk.transform
    def forward(emb, mask):
      transformer = model.Transformer(
          model.TransformerConfig(
              num_heads=1,
              num_layers=1,
              key_size=2,
              mlp_hidden_size=8,
              dropout_rate=0.,
              layer_norm=False,
              causal=True))
      return transformer(emb, mask).output

    emb = jnp.ones((1, 3, 1))
    mask = jnp.ones((1, 3))
    rng = hk.PRNGSequence(0)
    params = forward.init(next(rng), emb, mask)
    params = self._zero_mlps(params)
    out = forward.apply(params, next(rng), emb, mask)
    # With causal masking and identical inputs, first position only attends
    # to itself, while later positions attend to more positions, so outputs
    # should differ.
    self.assertFalse(jnp.allclose(out[0, 0], out[0, 1]))
    self.assertFalse(jnp.allclose(out[0, 1], out[0, 2]))

    def __call__(self, state_dict: Dict):
        """

        """

        # Replaces only first occurences
        all_keys = set(state_dict.keys())

        include_keys = set(state_dict.keys())
        if self.key_pattern is not None:

                self.key_pattern, state_dict.keys()
            )

        excluded_keys = all_keys - include_keys

        # Add excluded keys from re-mapping
        new_state_dict = {}
        for k in excluded_keys:
            new_state_dict[k] = state_dict[k]

        # Add keys from remapping
        for key in include_keys:

def _adstock_scan(
      carry: jnp.ndarray, x: jnp.ndarray) -> tuple[jnp.ndarray, jnp.ndarray]:
    new_carry = carry * lag_weight + x
    return new_carry, new_carry

  init_carry = jnp.zeros(shape=data.shape[1:])
  # Transpose to scan over time axis (axis 0).
  if data.ndim == 3:
    # Scan over time, vmap over geos is handled by scanning with
    # matching leading dims: flatten media and geo into one axis.
    # data shape: (time, media, geo)
    def _scan_media_geo(carry, x):
      new_carry = carry * lag_weight + x
      return new_carry, new_carry
    _, result = jax.lax.scan(_scan_media_geo, init_carry, data)
  else:
    _, result = jax.lax.scan(_adstock_scan, init_carry, data)

  if normalise:
    result = result * (1.0 - lag_weight)
  return result


def adstock(
    data: jnp.ndarray,
    custom_priors: Mapping[str, dist.Distribution],
    *,
    normalise: bool = True,
    prefix: str = "",
) -> jnp.ndarray:
  """Transforms the input data with the adstock function.

  Args:
    data: Media data to be transformed. It is expected to have 2 dims for
      national models and 3 for geo models.
    custom_priors: The custom priors we want the model to take instead of the
      default ones.
    normalise: Whether to normalise the output value.
    prefix: Prefix to use in the variable name for Numpyro.

  Returns:
    The transformed media data.
  """
  default_priors = priors.get_default_priors()
  with numpyro.plate(
      name=f"{prefix}{priors.LAG_WEIGHT}_plate", size=data.shape[1]):
    lag_weight = numpyro.sample(
        name=f"{prefix}{priors.LAG_WEIGHT}",
        fn=custom_priors.get(priors.LAG_WEIGHT,
                             default_priors[priors.LAG_WEIGHT]))

  return _adstock(data=data, lag_weight=lag_weight, normalise=normalise)

def adstock_internal(
      prev_adstock: jnp.ndarray,
      data: jnp.ndarray,
      lag_weight: Union[float, jnp.ndarray] = lag_weight,
  ) -> jnp.ndarray:
    adstock_value = prev_adstock * lag_weight + data
    return adstock_value, adstock_value# jax-ndarray

  _, adstock_values = jax.lax.scan(
      f=adstock_internal, init=data[0, ...], xs=data[1:, ...])
  adstock_values = jnp.concatenate([jnp.array([data[0, ...]]), adstock_values])
  return jax.lax.cond(
      normalise,
      lambda adstock_values: adstock_values / (1. / (1 - lag_weight)),
      lambda adstock_values: adstock_values,
      operand=adstock_values)

def _estimate_prior(p: jnp.ndarray,
                    x: jnp.ndarray,
                    discrete: bool = False) -> jnp.ndarray:
  """Estimates prior density.

  Args:
    p: Samples.
    x: The x space (sorted).
    discrete: Whether the variable is discrete.

  Returns:
    A density vector.
  """
  if discrete:
    return _pmf(p, x)
  return _estimate_pdf(p, x)


def _plot_prior(ax: plt.Axes,
                prior_samples: jnp.ndarray,
                x: jnp.ndarray,
                discrete: bool = False) -> plt.Axes:
  """Plots prior density.

  Args:
    ax: Matplotlib axes.
    prior_samples: Samples from prior.
    x: The x space (sorted).
    discrete: Whether the variable is discrete.

  Returns:
    Matplotlib axes.
  """
  density = _estimate_prior(prior_samples, x, discrete)
  if discrete:
    ax.stem(x, density, use_line_collection=True)
  else:
    ax.plot(x, density)
  return ax


def plot_prior(prior_samples: Dict[str, jnp.ndarray],
               n_cols: int = 3) -> plt.Figure:
  """Plots prior distributions.

  Args:
    prior_samples: Dictionary of prior samples keyed by parameter name.
    n_cols: Number of columns in the plot grid.

  Returns:
    Matplotlib figure.
  """
  n_params = len(prior_samples)
  n_rows = int(np.ceil(n_params / n_cols))
  fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_rows, n_cols, figsize=(n_cols * 4, n_rows * 3))
  axes = np.ravel(axes)
  for ax, (name, p) in zip(axes, prior_samples.items()):
    p = np.asarray(p).ravel()
    if np.all(np.mod(p, 1) == 0):
      x = np.unique(p)
      discrete = True
    else:
      x = np.linspace(np.min(p), np.max(p), 100)
      discrete = False
    _plot_prior(ax, p, x, discrete)
    ax.set_title(name)
  fig.tight_layout()
  return fig


def plot_model_fit(media_mix_model,
                   target_scaler=None) -> plt.Figure:
  """Plots model fit.

  Args:
    media_mix_model: Media mix model with predictions.
    target_scaler: Scaler for target to invert scaling.

  Returns:
    Matplotlib figure.
  """
  fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))
  target = np.asarray(media_mix_model._target)
  prediction = np.asarray(media_mix_model._prediction.mean(axis=0))
  if target_scaler is not None:
    target = target_scaler.inverse_transform(target)
    prediction = target_scaler.inverse_transform(prediction)
  if target.ndim == 2:
    target = target.sum(axis=1)
    prediction = prediction.sum(axis=1)
  ax.plot(target, label="Actual")
  ax.plot(prediction, label="Predicted")
  ax.legend()
  ax.set_xlabel("Time")
  ax.set_ylabel("Target")
  fig.tight_layout()
  return fig

                         media_scaler=None,
                         target_scaler=None,
                         n_points: int = 100) -> plt.Figure:
  """Plots response curves.

  Args:
    media_mix_model: Fitted media mix model.

    target_scaler: Scaler for target to invert scaling.

    y = np.asarray(media_mix_model.get_response_curve(x, i).mean(axis=0))

    ax.set_xlabel("Media units")

  fig.tight_layout()

@jax.jit
def hill(data: jnp.ndarray, half_max_effective_concentration: jnp.ndarray,
         slope: jnp.ndarray) -> jnp.ndarray:
  """Calculates the hill function for a given array of values.

  Refer to the following link for detailed information on this equation:
    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hill_equation_(biochemistry)

  Args:
    data: Input array.
    half_max_effective_concentration: Control for the half maximum effective
      concentration.
    slope: Control for the slope of the hill function.

  Returns:
    The hill output of the input array.
  """
  return 1. / (1. + (data / half_max_effective_concentration) ** -slope)

        out = einsum('... i j, ... j d -> ... i d', attn, v)
        out = rearrange(out, 'b h n d -> b n (h d)')
        return self.to_out(out)

  def _evaluate_tokens(self, expr: Tokens,
                       xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    return list(xs)

  def _evaluate_indices(self, expr: Indices,
                        xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    return list(range(len(xs)))

  def _evaluate_length(self, expr: Length,
                       xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    return [len(xs)] * len(xs)

  def _evaluate_select(self, expr: Select,
                       xs: Sequence[Value]) -> SelectorValue:
    keys = self.evaluate(expr.keys, xs)
    queries = self.evaluate(expr.queries, xs)
    return [[bool(expr.predicate(k, q)) for k in keys] for q in queries]

  def _evaluate_selector_and(self, expr: SelectorAnd,
                             xs: Sequence[Value]) -> SelectorValue:
    fst = self.evaluate(expr.fst, xs)
    snd = self.evaluate(expr.snd, xs)
    return [[a and b for a, b in zip(fst_row, snd_row)]
            for fst_row, snd_row in zip(fst, snd)]

  def _evaluate_selector_or(self, expr: SelectorOr,
                            xs: Sequence[Value]) -> SelectorValue:
    fst = self.evaluate(expr.fst, xs)
    snd = self.evaluate(expr.snd, xs)
    return [[a or b for a, b in zip(fst_row, snd_row)]
            for fst_row, snd_row in zip(fst, snd)]

  def _evaluate_selector_not(self, expr: SelectorNot,
                             xs: Sequence[Value]) -> SelectorValue:
    inner = self.evaluate(expr.inner, xs)
    return [[not b for b in row] for row in inner]

  def _evaluate_constant_selector(self, expr: ConstantSelector,
                                  xs: Sequence[Value]) -> SelectorValue:
    return [[expr.value] * len(xs) for _ in xs]

  def _evaluate_aggregate(self, expr: Aggregate,
                          xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    selector = self.evaluate(expr.selector, xs)
    sop = self.evaluate(expr.sop, xs)
    out = []
    for row in selector:
      selected = [v for v, b in zip(sop, row) if b]
      if selected:
        out.append(sum(selected) / len(selected))
      else:
        if expr.default is None:
          raise ValueError("No value selected and no default provided.")
        out.append(expr.default)
    return out

  def _evaluate_selector_width(self, expr: SelectorWidth,
                               xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    selector = self.evaluate(expr.selector, xs)
    return [sum(row) for row in selector]

  def _evaluate_map(self, expr: Map,
                    xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    inner = self.evaluate(expr.inner, xs)
    return [expr.f(x) for x in inner]

  def _evaluate_sequence_map(self, expr: SequenceMap,
                             xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    evaluated = [self.evaluate(inner, xs) for inner in expr.inners]
    return [expr.f(*vals) for vals in zip(*evaluated)]

  def _evaluate_linear_sequence_map(self, expr: LinearSequenceMap,
                                    xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    evaluated = [self.evaluate(inner, xs) for inner in expr.inners]
    return [sum(w * v for w, v in zip(expr.weights, vals)) + expr.bias
            for vals in zip(*evaluated)]

  def _evaluate_full(self, expr: Full,
                     xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    return [expr.fill] * len(xs)

  def _evaluate_constant_sop(self, expr: ConstantSOp,
                             xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    return list(expr.value)

@dataclasses.dataclass
class SeriesBlock(Block):
  """Applies blocks in series, with residual connections."""
  sub_blocks: List[Block]

  def __post_init__(self):
    spaces = [block.residual_space for block in self.sub_blocks]
    self.residual_space, *others = spaces
    assert all(s == self.residual_space for s in others)

  def apply(self, x: bases.VectorInBasis) -> bases.VectorInBasis:
    assert x in self.residual_space
    for block in self.sub_blocks:
      x = x + block.apply(x)
    return x

    def __call__(self, state_dict: Dict):
        """

            state_dict: A dictionary representing the given checkpoint's state dict.

        include_keys = set(state_dict.keys())

            include_keys = _unix_pattern_to_parameter_names(
                self.key_pattern, state_dict.keys()
            )

        excluded_keys = all_keys - include_keys

        # Add excluded keys from re-mapping
        new_state_dict = {}
        for k in excluded_keys:
            new_state_dict[k] = state_dict[k]

        # Add keys from remapping
        for key in include_keys:
            for target_pattern in self.target_patterns:
                new_key = key.replace(
                    self.source_pattern, target_pattern, 1
                )
                new_state_dict[new_key] = state_dict[key]

def adstock(
    data: jnp.ndarray,
    custom_priors: Mapping[str, dist.Distribution],
    *,
    prefix: str = "",
) -> jnp.ndarray:
  """Transforms the input data with the adstock function.

  Args:
    data: Media data to be transformed. It is expected to have 2 dims for
      national models and 3 for geo models.
    custom_priors: The custom priors we want the model to take instead of the
      default ones.
    prefix: Prefix to use in the variable name for Numpyro.

  Returns:
    The transformed media data.
  """
  default_priors = priors.get_default_priors()
  with numpyro.plate(
      name=f"{prefix}{priors.LAG_WEIGHT}_plate", size=data.shape[1]):
    lag_weight = numpyro.sample(
        name=f"{prefix}{priors.LAG_WEIGHT}",
        fn=custom_priors.get(priors.LAG_WEIGHT,
                             default_priors[priors.LAG_WEIGHT]))

  return _adstock(data=data, lag_weight=lag_weight)

  def _objective(b: float, mu: float, sigma: float) -> float:
    a = mu * b / (1. - mu)
    var = a * b / ((a + b) ** 2 * (a + b + 1.))
    return np.sqrt(var) - sigma

  a = mu * b / (1. - mu)
  return a, b

  def fit(
      self,
      media: jnp.ndarray,
      target: jnp.ndarray,
      extra_features: Optional[jnp.ndarray] = None,
      media_prior: Optional[jnp.ndarray] = None,
      degrees_seasonality: int = 2,
      weekday_seasonality: bool = False,
      media_names: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
      custom_priors: Optional[MutableMapping[str, Prior]] = None,
      number_warmup: int = 1000,
      number_samples: int = 1000,
      number_chains: int = 1,
      target_is_log_scale: bool = False,
      seed: int = 0,
      **kwargs) -> None:
    """Fits media mix model.

    Args:
      media: Media data with shape (time, media_channels) for national models
        or (geos, time, media_channels) for geo models.
      target: Target data with shape (time,) for national models or
        (geos, time) for geo models.
      extra_features: Extra features data with shape (time, features) for
        national models or (geos, time, features) for geo models.
      media_prior: Cost or prior weight of each media channel with shape
        (media_channels,).
      degrees_seasonality: Degrees of seasonality.
      weekday_seasonality: Whether to include weekday seasonality.
      media_names: Names of the media channels.
      custom_priors: Custom priors for the model.
      number_warmup: Number of warmup samples.
      number_samples: Number of samples.
      number_chains: Number of chains.
      target_is_log_scale: Whether the target is in log scale.
      seed: Random seed.
      **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments to pass to the MCMC sampler.

    Raises:
      ValueError: If the media and target shapes are not compatible.
    """
    if media.ndim == 2:
      self.n_geos = 1
      media = media[jnp.newaxis, ...]
      target = target[jnp.newaxis, ...] if target.ndim == 1 else target
      if extra_features is not None and extra_features.ndim == 2:
        extra_features = extra_features[jnp.newaxis, ...]
    elif media.ndim == 3:
      self.n_geos = media.shape[0]
    else:
      raise ValueError("Media data must have 2 or 3 dimensions.")

    self.n_media_channels = media.shape[-1]
    self._train_media_size = media.shape[1]
    self.media = media[0] if self.n_geos == 1 else media
    self._target = target
    self._extra_features = extra_features
    self._degrees_seasonality = degrees_seasonality
    self._weekday_seasonality = weekday_seasonality
    self.media_names = (
        media_names if media_names is not None else
        [f"channel_{i}" for i in range(self.n_media_channels)])
    self.custom_priors = custom_priors if custom_priors is not None else {}
    self._media_prior = (
        media_prior if media_prior is not None else jnp.ones(
            self.n_media_channels) / self.n_media_channels)

    model_kwargs = {
        "media_data": media,
        "extra_features": extra_features,
        "degrees_seasonality": degrees_seasonality,
        "weekday_seasonality": weekday_seasonality,
        "media_prior": self._media_prior,
        "custom_priors": self.custom_priors,
        "model_name": self.model_name,
    }

    mcmc = infer.MCMC(
        infer.NUTS(self._model_function),
        num_warmup=number_warmup,
        num_samples=number_samples,
        num_chains=number_chains,
        progress_bar=False,
        **kwargs)
    rng_key = jax.random.PRNGKey(seed)
    mcmc.run(rng_key, target, **model_kwargs)
    self._mcmc = mcmc
    self.trace = mcmc.get_samples()

  def predict(
      self,
      media: jnp.ndarray,
      extra_features: Optional[jnp.ndarray] = None,
      seed: int = 0) -> jnp.ndarray:
    """Predicts target for given media and extra features.

    Args:
      media: Media data with shape (time, media_channels) or
        (geos, time, media_channels).
      extra_features: Extra features data.
      seed: Random seed.

    Returns:
      Predictions with shape (samples, time) or (samples, geos, time).

    Raises:
      NotFittedModelError: If the model has not been fitted.
    """
    if not hasattr(self, "trace"):
      raise NotFittedModelError(
          "Model has not been fitted. Call fit() first.")
    if media.ndim == 2:
      media = media[jnp.newaxis, ...]
      if extra_features is not None and extra_features.ndim == 2:
        extra_features = extra_features[jnp.newaxis, ...]
    predictive = infer.Predictive(
        self._model_function,
        posterior_samples=self.trace,
        return_sites=["y_hat"])
    rng_key = jax.random.PRNGKey(seed)
    preds = predictive(
        rng_key,
        jnp.zeros((media.shape[0], media.shape[1])),
        media_data=media,
        extra_features=extra_features,
        degrees_seasonality=self._degrees_seasonality,
        weekday_seasonality=self._weekday_seasonality,
        media_prior=self._media_prior,
        custom_priors=self.custom_priors,
        model_name=self.model_name)["y_hat"]
    return preds[:, 0, :] if self.n_geos == 1 else preds

  def get_posterior_metrics(
      self,
      unscaled_costs: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None) -> Tuple[jnp.ndarray,
                                                                jnp.ndarray,
                                                                jnp.ndarray]:
    """Gets posterior predictions, media contribution and ROI.

    Args:
      unscaled_costs: Unscaled costs for ROI calculation. If None, uses
        media_prior scaled by media sums.

    Returns:
      Tuple of predictions, media contribution percentage and ROI.
    """
    if not hasattr(self, "trace"):
      raise NotFittedModelError(
          "Model has not been fitted. Call fit() first.")
    predictions = utils.get_predictions_from_trace(
        trace=self.trace,
        media=self.media if self.n_geos == 1 else self.media,
        extra_features=self._extra_features,
        degrees_seasonality=self._degrees_seasonality,
        weekday_seasonality=self._weekday_seasonality,
        media_prior=self._media_prior,
        model_name=self.model_name,
        transform_function=self._model_transform_function)
    media_contribution, roi = utils.get_media_contribution_and_roi(
        trace=self.trace,
        media=self.media,
        transform_function=self._model_transform_function,
        unscaled_costs=unscaled_costs)
    return predictions, media_contribution, roi

  def eval_constant_sop(self, sop: ConstantSOp,
                        xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    return [sop.value] * len(xs)

  def eval_selector_width(self, sop: SelectorWidth,
                          xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[int]:
    selector_value = self.evaluate(sop.selector, xs)
    return [sum(row) for row in selector_value]

  def eval_aggregate(self, sop: Aggregate,
                     xs: Sequence[Value]) -> Sequence[Value]:
    selector_value = self.evaluate(sop.selector, xs)
    sop_values = self.evaluate(sop.sop, xs)
    out = []
    for row in selector_value:
      selected = [v for s, v in zip(row, sop_values) if s]
      selected = [v for v in selected if v is not None]
      if selected:
        # Average for numerical, else take most common / first?
        # Default RASP aggregate averages numerical values.
        if isinstance(selected[0], bool):
          out.append(sum(selected) / len(selected))
        elif isinstance(selected[0], (int, float)):
          out.append(sum(selected) / len(selected))
        else:
          # For categorical, take the selected value (must be unique).
          # If multiple distinct values, take first.
          out.append(selected[0])
      else:
        out.append(sop.default)
    return out

  def eval_select(self, sop: Select,
                  xs: Sequence[Value]) -> SelectorValue:
    if isinstance(sop.keys, Full):
      keys = [sop.keys.fill] * len(xs)
    else:
      keys = self.evaluate(sop.keys, xs)
    if isinstance(sop.queries, Full):
      queries = [sop.queries.fill] * len(xs)
    else:
      queries = self.evaluate(sop.queries, xs)
    return [[bool(sop.predicate(k, q)) if k is not None and q is not None
             else False for k in keys] for q in queries]

  def eval_selector_and(self, sop: SelectorAnd,
                        xs: Sequence[Value]) -> SelectorValue:
    fst = self.evaluate(sop.fst, xs)
    snd = self.evaluate(sop.snd, xs)
    return [[a and b for a, b in zip(fst_row, snd_row)]
            for fst_row, snd_row in zip(fst, snd)]

  def eval_selector_or(self, sop: SelectorOr,
                       xs: Sequence[Value]) -> SelectorValue:
    fst = self.evaluate(sop.fst, xs)
    snd = self.evaluate(sop.snd, xs)
    return [[a or b for a, b in zip(fst_row, snd_row)]
            for fst_row, snd_row in zip(fst, snd)]

  def eval_selector_not(self, sop: SelectorNot,
                        xs: Sequence[Value]) -> SelectorValue:
    inner = self.evaluate(sop.inner, xs)
    return [[not v for v in row] for row in inner]

  def eval_constant_selector(self, sop: ConstantSelector,
                             xs: Sequence[Value]) -> SelectorValue:
    n = len(xs)
    return [[sop.value] * n for _ in range(n)]

  def __call__(
      self,
      tokens: jax.Array,  # [B, T]
      *,
      use_dropout: bool = True,
  ) -> CompiledTransformerModelOutput:
    """Transforms input token sequences to output token sequences."""
    if self.pad_token is None:
      mask = jnp.ones_like(tokens)
    else:
      mask = (tokens != self.pad_token).astype(jnp.float32)
    embeddings = self.embed(tokens)
    transformer_output = self.transformer(
        embeddings, mask, use_dropout=use_dropout)
    unembedded_output = self.unembed(transformer_output.output)
    if self.use_unembed_argmax:
      unembedded_output = jnp.argmax(unembedded_output, axis=-1)
    return CompiledTransformerModelOutput(
        transformer_output=transformer_output,
        unembedded_output=unembedded_output,
    )

    # To compress the model, we multiply with a matrix W when reading from

    if embedding_size is not None:
      # [to_size, from_size]
      w_emb = hk.get_parameter(
          "w_emb", (embedding_size, model_size),
          init=hk.initializers.RandomNormal())

      write_to_residual = lambda x: x @ w_emb.T
      read_from_residual = lambda x: x @ w_emb

      if not unembed_at_every_layer:
        model_size = embedding_size
    else:
      write_to_residual = lambda x: x
      read_from_residual = lambda x: x

    # Compute causal mask for autoregressive sequence modelling.
    mask = mask[:, None, None, :]  # [B, H=1, T'=1, T]
    mask = mask.repeat(seq_len, axis=2)  # [B, H=1, T, T]

    if self.config.causal:
      causal_mask = np.ones((1, 1, seq_len, seq_len))  # [B=1, H=1, T, T]
      causal_mask = np.tril(causal_mask)
      mask = mask * causal_mask  # [B, H=1, T, T]

    # Set up activation collection.
    collected = collections.defaultdict(list)

    def collect(**kwargs):
      for k, v in kwargs.items():
        collected[k].append(v)

    residual = write_to_residual(embeddings)
    for layer in range(self.config.num_layers):
      with hk.experimental.name_scope(f"layer_{layer}"):
        # First the attention block.
        attn_block = attention.MultiHeadAttention(
            num_heads=self.config.num_heads,
            key_size=self.config.key_size,
            model_size=model_size,
            w_init=initializer,
        )
        if unembed_at_every_layer:
          attn_input = read_from_residual(layer_norm(residual))
        else:
          attn_input = layer_norm(residual)
        attn_out, attn_logits = attn_block(
            attn_input, attn_input, attn_input, mask)
        attn_out = hk.dropout(hk.next_rng_key(), dropout_rate, attn_out)
        residual = residual + write_to_residual(attn_out)
        collect(attn_logits=attn_logits, residuals=residual)

        # Then the MLP block.
        mlp_block = model.MLP(
            widening_factor=self.config.widening_factor,
            model_size=model_size,
            w_init=initializer,
        )
        if unembed_at_every_layer:

        else:

        mlp_out = mlp_block(mlp_input)
        mlp_out = hk.dropout(hk.next_rng_key(), dropout_rate, mlp_out)
        residual = residual + write_to_residual(mlp_out)
        collect(layer_outputs=residual, residuals=residual)

        layer_outputs=collected["layer_outputs"],
        residuals=collected["residuals"],
        attn_logits=collected["attn_logits"],

# Embeds tokens as one-hot into the first `vocab_size` dimensions
    # and positions as one-hot into the next `max_seq_len` dimensions.
    def embed(tokens):
      token_emb = jax.nn.one_hot(tokens, vocab_size)
      pos = jnp.arange(tokens.shape[-1])
      pos_emb = jax.nn.one_hot(pos, max_seq_len)
      pos_emb = jnp.broadcast_to(pos_emb, token_emb.shape[:-1] + (max_seq_len,))
      return jnp.concatenate([token_emb, pos_emb], axis=-1)

    def unembed(x):
      return jnp.dot(x, jnp.eye(x.shape[-1], vocab_size))

    return embed, unembed

@jax.jit
def hill(data: jnp.ndarray, half_max_effective_concentration: jnp.ndarray,
         slope: jnp.ndarray) -> jnp.ndarray:
  """Calculates the hill function for a given array of values.

  Refer to the following link for detailed information on this equation:
    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hill_equation_(biochemistry)

  Args:
    data: Input array.
    half_max_effective_concentration: Half max effective concentration. This is
      the value at which the function reaches half of its max value.
    slope: Slope of the hill function.

  Returns:
    The hill output of the input array.
  """
  return 1. / (1. + (data / half_max_effective_concentration) ** -slope)

    result = optimize_media.find_optimal_budgets(
        media_mix_model=self.national_mmm,
        budget=100.,
        bounds=bounds,
